title: Bridges between groups
question: Which organizations, firms, people or addresses connect two otherwise separate flagged groups?
finding: 70 members or neighbours touch two or more groups. Yes on G, the Affordable Housing Opportunity Fund touches the most (7): 3. Chinatown Community Development Center; 4. Young Community Developers Inc; 9. Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corp; 10. Mission Neighborhood Health Center; 17. Mission Economic Development Agency; 21. The SF Housing Accelerator Fund; and 1 more. 38 of them are the only tie found between at least one pair of groups.
how: For every node left in the graph, the groups it belongs to and the groups its direct neighbours belong to were counted. A node that touches two or more groups is a bridge. "Only tie" counts the pairs of groups for which no other bridge was found. Built on the graph described under “The linked groups”: organizations, firms, San Francisco addresses and people (officers, registered lobbyists and consultants, officials) joined by eleven kinds of recorded link, each with its source. Public bodies, banks, utilities, insurers, law and accounting firms, universities, hospitals, office buildings, and any node tied to more than 12 others by one kind of link were removed first. A person appears only on a rare full name, in a public role on file, with a second independent record for each tie, and is always a name match. A member is called a party only if the record of case outcomes lists it as one; being named in a case file is shown separately. Groups are the connected sets that remain, or the tightly linked cores of sets larger than 40.
limits: Being linked is not being involved: nonprofits share board members, buildings and auditors all the time, and San Francisco is a small city. A group is a place to look, ranked by how many independent signs sit inside it. A bridge is often the most ordinary member of all: a supervisor who asked for donations to several neighbourhood groups, a nonprofit centre with many tenants, a funder, a board member who serves two organizations. Hubs tied to more than 12 others by one kind of link were removed before this was run, so the busiest connectors are in the removed list, not here. Payment at an official's request: officials must disclose charitable payments they ask for. Shares an officer or director (name match): board members often serve several organizations, and affiliates share leaders as a matter of course. Same street address: nonprofit centres, landlords and tenants, and fiscal sponsors share buildings. Gives to the campaign of: campaign donations are reported, with limits on amounts.
